overview: White opens 1.b3 and Black meets it with the Dutch-style 1...f5. White continues 2.Bb2 Nf6 3.e3 (often followed by Nf3, Be2 or Bb5-style ideas) and aims the b2-bishop at e5 and g7. The game is a flexible hypermodern fight where White controls e5 and Black builds a Stonewall or Dutch-like formation.

white_ideas.idea: Play Bb2, e3, Nf3 and keep the e5 square under control
Use the bishop on b2 against Black's kingside and prepare f4 or c4 depending on the set-up

black_ideas.idea: Aim for ...e5 or kingside play with ...f4 once the bishops are placed

typical_structures.structure: Dutch pawn on f5 against a White pawn set-up on b3/e3 with a fianchettoed bishop on b2

character.notes: Slow development battle with low theory and no forcing lines; neither solid nor sharp: Balanced.

structure.notes: Pawn structure stays flexible, with e5 contested by pieces; Flexible.

approach.notes: White plays the same b3/Bb2/e3/Nf3 pieces against almost every defence, which is System-like; the parent is a surprise weapon for super-GMs.

level.notes: Few forced lines; plans are clear but the Dutch structure takes understanding. Intermediate.

character.reason: A slow flank opening against a Dutch with neither forcing play nor a rock-solid structure.

soundness.reason: A normal, safe set-up for both.

structure.reason: A flank opening with the centre undecided.

approach.reason: White's b3/Bb2/e3/Nf3 set-up is played against almost anything.

level.reason: Plans are simple but the middlegame needs judgement.

plans.reason: Bb2 on the long diagonal and control of the centre from the flank.
